en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Universal Radiance Treasury Free from Words, translated by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
There were great bodhisattvas numbering in the hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas—all of whom possessed great wisdom, diligence, and skillful means;
who had realized the ineffable Dharma and attained sublime eloquence; who did not contradict the principles of what is possible and what is impossible;
who were well-disciplined in body and mind and endowed with all liberations; who constantly dwelled in samādhi and never abandoned great compassion; and who were possessed of a sense of shame...
Taking shame as the foundation and wisdom as the foremost, they are of great benefit like a great jewel island;

they thoroughly understand the characteristics of all phenomena, both wholesome and unwholesome; they employ verbal expression without clinging to words; they penetrate the gates of the ultimate and the conventional without obstruction;
they deeply realize the reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) yet do not abide within it; and they are skillfully able to discern all things without [conceptual] attachment.
Although he has grown weary of birth and death, he constantly protects the world;

his great fame pervades the ten directions, and he rests in tranquil repose within the truly wondrous treasury. Although he manifests the taking of a body, he has forever transcended the three realms;

yet he traverses all states of existence to diligently rescue sentient beings, instructing them with impartiality while his will remains ever virtuous and good, and he regards them all with equal compassion.
With a mind free from defilement and attachment, they are able to bring both themselves and others to complete purity, accomplishing such immeasurable merits—
namely: the Bodhisattva Supreme Reflection, the Bodhisattva Sound-Shaking Dharma,

the Bodhisattva Wondrous Body, the Bodhisattva Dharma-Wheel Rim, the Bodhisattva Accumulated Eloquence, the Bodhisattva Sustaining the Earth, the Bodhisattva Sustaining the World, the Bodhisattva Great Renown, the Bodhisattva Endowed with All Eloquence, the Bodhisattva Thousand-Auspicious-Marks, the Bodhisattva Mountain of Merit, the Bodhisattva Lotus-Eye, the Bodhisattva Lotus-Face, the Bodhisattva Jewel-Crest, and the Bodhisattva Wondrous Voice.
These and other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were all like youths, with countenances of exquisite and dignified beauty, serving as the leaders within this assembly.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was accompanied by bodhisattvas who had succeeded to the position of the Honored One, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
the Bodhisattva Viśiṣṭadarśana was accompanied by countless Śakras, the lords of the devas.
The Bodhisattva Gaganagañja was accompanied by immeasurable bodhisattvas and immeasurable hosts of the Four Great Kings;
the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta was accompanied by immeasurable billions of Brahmās;
and the Bodhisattva Samantasaubhāgya was accompanied by immeasurable court ladies.

Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Amoghadarśin Bodhisattva, Jyotirāja Bodhisattva, Vigatasaṃśaya Bodhisattva, Sarvāvaraṇavikiraṇa Bodhisattva, Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata Bodhisattva were each accompanied by an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas;
among them were also immeasurable buddhas who had themselves transformed their bodies into the forms of bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, the Venerable Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, and other such great arhats were each accompanied by an immeasurable assembly of śrāvakas.

Immeasurable hosts of devas, such as Nārāyaṇa and others, even down to the sun and moon deities from lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all came to the Buddha’s presence with their majestic radiance shining forth.
Once they had arrived at the Buddha’s presence, the majestic light of those devas could no longer manifest; it was like a mass of ink set against Jambūnada gold.

The Naga King Varuṇa, the Naga King Takṣaka, the Naga King Anavatapta, the Gandharva King Manojña-ghoṣa, and the Garuḍa King An-ākulita, each accompanied by immeasurable retinues, entered this assembly.

All the bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each requested the Tathāgata in their own native lands to come; together with the fourfold assembly, they arrived here simultaneously. Each holding various kinds of extraordinary and excellent offerings surpassing those of the world, they presented them to the Buddha and the bodhisattvas, and then sat upon lotus seats within the assembly.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Viśeṣacintin rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
“World-Honored One!
"I now wish to inquire about the meaning of these two characters; I only pray that the Tathāgata will look upon me with compassion and grant me permission.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin, saying:
"Good son!..."

If there is anyone who wishes to ask a question, let them ask according to their own inclination; it is not for the sake of a single sentient being that the Tathāgata appears in the world, but rather for the purpose of benefiting immeasurable sentient beings that he has appeared!
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Victorious Contemplation addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is that single dharma which all bodhisattvas should forever abandon?”
“What is that one dharma which all bodhisattvas should constantly protect and uphold?
What is that one dharma which all Tathāgatas have currently awakened to?
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family,
it is by the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata that you are able to question me on such a profound meaning.”
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well!
I shall speak for your sake. "Good son!
There is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, sensual desire.
Good son! Such a dharma as this is what all bodhisattvas should forever abandon.
"Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, anger; such a dharma as this is what all bodhisattvas should forever abandon."
"Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, ignorance; this one dharma is what all bodhisattvas should forever abandon."
"Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, the grasping at a self.
Good son!"
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, doubt and hesitation.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, arrogance.
"Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, laziness.
Good son!"
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, torpor and drowsiness.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should abandon, namely, attachment and craving.
"Good son! This one dharma is that which all bodhisattvas should forever abandon. Good son!"
You have further asked me:
"What is that one dharma which all bodhisattvas should constantly protect and uphold?
Son of good family!
That is to say, Bodhisattvas do not impose upon others that which is not themselves at ease with.
If Bodhisattvas guard this Dharma, they are thereby able to uphold all the prohibitive precepts of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
Why is this? Because one who cherishes their own body and life should not kill;
one who values their own wealth and possessions should not steal.
One should protect one's own wife and not violate another's;
such practices as these are all called the "One Dharma. Good son!
If there are those who revere and comply with the Tathāgata’s words, they should constantly keep this one Dharma in mind. Why is this?

There are no sentient beings who delight in suffering; whatever they do, they seek only peace and happiness. Even when Bodhisattvas seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, it is for the sake of both themselves and others attaining happiness.
"Good son!

It is for this reason that I have spoken these words: one should not impose upon others what one does not find personally agreeable. This single dharma is that which all bodhisattvas should constantly protect and uphold."
“Good son! Regarding what you have asked:
‘What is the one dharma that all Tathāgatas have presently awakened to?’”
“Good son! There is not even the slightest dharma that the Tathāgata has awakened to. Why is this?
The Tathāgata’s awakening consists in having nothing to awaken to.
Son of good family!
That all phenomena are unborn is the Tathāgata’s awakening.
That all phenomena are without cessation is the Tathāgata’s awakening;
that all phenomena are free from the two extremes is the Tathāgata’s awakening;
that all phenomena are unreal is the Tathāgata’s awakening.
"Good son! That the intrinsic nature of all karmas is suchness is the Tathāgata’s awakening;
that all dharmas arise from causes and conditions is the Tathāgata’s awakening."
The dharma of causes and conditions is like a flash of lightning; this is the awakening of the Tathāgata.
Because of causes and conditions, various karmas come to be; this is the awakening of the Tathāgata. Good son!
The universal radiance treasury of the nature of all phenomena is the awakening of the Tathāgata.
Son of good family,
for what reason is the nature of phenomena called the universal radiance treasury?
"Good son! Worldly and world-transcending wisdoms arise in dependence upon it; like a mother carrying a child in her womb, it is therefore called a 'treasury' (garbha).
When wisdom arises, it reflects back upon its own source, and this very dharma-nature is encompassed and stored within Prajñāpāramitā; for this reason, it is called the Universal Radiance Treasury."
“Good son! That all dharmas are like illusions and like mirages—this is the awakening of the Tathāgata. Good son!”

The Tathāgata’s awakening is the single flavor of liberation, which is the true nature of all phenomena; this single flavor of liberation is precisely what is called the Universal Radiance Treasury. Good son!
The dharma of the single characteristic is that which the Tathāgata has awakened to.
What is the single characteristic?
It is that all dharmas neither come nor go, are neither causes nor conditions, are neither born nor extinguished, involve neither grasping nor abandoning, and neither increase nor decrease.
"Good son! The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is fundamentally non-existent and cannot be illustrated by analogy; it is not something that can be explained through words and phrases.
Such a single dharma is what all Tathāgatas have directly realized."

When the Buddha preached this Dharma-gate of the King of Adornments, the Universal Radiance Treasury Free from Words, there were sentient beings as numerous as the atoms perceived by a bodhisattva of the tenth stage who all resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, there were sentient beings as numerous as those atoms who all resolved their minds upon the paths of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Moreover, there were sentient beings as numerous as those atoms who, having been in the hells, were all freed from suffering and reborn among humans and devas.
Immeasurable bodhisattvas attained entry into the first stage; immeasurable bodhisattvas attained hundreds of thousands of samādhis;
and immeasurable sentient beings all received benefit, with none passing by in vain.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Rāhula, saying:
"Good son! You should receive and uphold this essential teaching of mine."

When these words were spoken, there were ninety billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the assembly who, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, immediately rose from their seats and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We vow to receive and uphold the essential teachings of the Tathāgata, so that during the final age in this Sahā world-system, we may encounter those who propagate and expound them.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there should be anyone capable of upholding this sutra, we shall provide protection for them, ensuring that all their aspirations are fulfilled.”
"Why is this? Because those who are able to uphold this sutra are vessels of the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the entire assembly and spoke these words:
"O virtuous ones!

This profound, extensive, and rare Dharma-gate that I have here proclaimed cannot be heard or received by sentient beings who possess only a small amount of roots of goodness. Those who are able to hear and receive it are, in effect, serving and making offerings to me, and they are also carrying the burden of unsurpassed bodhi."
This person shall attain unimpeded eloquence and will certainly be reborn in a pure buddha-field;
at the time of death, this person will certainly behold Amitābha Buddha and the assembly of bodhisattvas appearing before them.
Just as I am now here on Vulture Peak Mountain, surrounded by the assembly of bodhisattvas, so too shall they see me at the time of their death!
You should know that such a person has already attained the inexhaustible treasury of Dharma;
you should know that such a person attains the knowledge of past lives.
"You should know that such a person shall not fall into the evil realms. Good son!

I now proclaim this Dharma which is difficult for all the world to believe. Should there be sentient beings who have committed the five heinous crimes, once they hear this sutra and subsequently copy, uphold, read, recite, or explain it to others, all their karmic obstructions shall be completely eliminated. They shall never suffer the pains of the evil destinies; such persons will be protected and remembered by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. In every place where they are born, their faculties will be complete, and they will receive the Buddha’s empowerment with the five eyes purified."
"Good son! To state the essential point, I see that such a person has already accomplished the Buddha-way.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, all the bodhisattvas, including Viśeṣacintī, as well as the śrāvakas, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings, were filled with great joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Universal Radiance Treasury Free from Words and Letters.
